stories.title: Korea's top tax-exam scorer admits cheating with a tiny camera and generative AI; state exam body files complaint
stories.notes: Anonymised in the article (Mr. A); do not name him. Korean-language source (facts translated). Yonhap/Korea Herald originals returned 403 or were not found. Previous run skipped this when it was still an allegation; it is now a self-admission and a police report. Related: PM vows to block AI cheating at the CSAT college exam (Yonhap/Korea Herald, unread), CSAT is days away.

articles.title: 세무사 시험 수석 합격자 "생성 AI로 부정행위" 자백

facts.text: The top passer of the 63rd tax accountant exam in Korea said he cheated using a micro camera and generative AI.
He said he photographed exam questions with the micro camera, sent them to AI and read the answers on a smartphone.
He said he used the same method on the first-round certified public accountant (CPA) exam, which he failed this year.
In April's first-round tax exam he missed only one of 160 questions; he then topped the July second round.
The Human Resources Development Service of Korea (HRDK), which runs the exam, earlier found nothing suspicious from its proctors.
On the 15th the HRDK apologised, said it will file a complaint for obstruction of business, seek to cancel his pass and check other national exams.
The Ministry of Finance and Economy is considering suspending the pass; police began an investigation after receiving his self-report.
He did not disclose the AI model or equipment used, saying details could enable repeats, and will tell investigators only.

stories.title: US, Korea, Japan and six others sign 'San Francisco Declaration' to protect AI supply chains (Pax Silica)
stories.notes: Original is FT interview with US Under Secretary Jacob Helberg (unreadable); cited via AI Times. Korean-language source. Signing comes before the Trump-Xi meeting on the 19th in Shenzhen.

articles.outlet: AI Times (Korea), citing the Financial Times
articles.title: 미국·한국 등 9개국, 중국 견제 AI 공급망 보호 공동 선언

facts.text: Nine countries signed the 'San Francisco Declaration' to protect AI supply chains: the US, Korea, Japan, Australia, Israel, UK, India, Qatar and the UAE, per the FT.
Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission are expected to sign next week.
It is part of the US-led AI supply chain initiative Pax Silica.
Members will jointly pick sensitive AI technologies and infrastructure to protect and share information on where supply chains need diversifying.
Helberg said the chip design technology, manufacturing equipment and shipping ports can each be in different countries, and the declaration treats their security as a shared responsibility.
Working groups will also set up economic hubs to attract AI investment.
The declaration announces no new export controls or legally binding rules.
It came ahead of the Trump-Xi talks at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on the 19th.

stories.title: Reuters: China has over 23B yuan in projects built on export-restricted Nvidia chips, now at risk
stories.notes: Reuters original not read; cited via AI Times (Korean). Won mention Huang only as export-policy context, not the scandal.

articles.title: 중국, 젠슨 황 사임·미국 규제 강화에 4조원대 AI 데이터센터 사업 위기

facts.text: Reuters reviewed more than 150 Chinese procurement notices, investment plans, construction contracts and company filings.
Projects and equipment contracts built on Nvidia's export-restricted processors total over 23 billion yuan (about 4.2 trillion won).
The chips are H100, H200 and H800, which are subject to US export restrictions.
Xianyou county in Fujian is pursuing a 6.2 billion yuan AI computing center using H100s and is still seeking partners.

Inner Mongolia plans a 1.5 billion yuan data center with 625 H200 servers; Gansu signed a 1.16 billion yuan contract for about 3,072 Nvidia processors; it is unconfirmed whether the chips were delivered.
The US has restricted advanced AI chip exports to China since 2022; in January it moved H200 to case-by-case licensing.
The article says no evidence links these projects to the Huang resignation or the Megaspeed controversy, and none is confirmed halted.

stories.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its AI agents (Dots) can shop for you, US Pro only
stories.notes: Runner-up from 11-15 morning and evening lists. heise (Germany) article read; OpenAI/TechCrunch/TNW originals not read this run. Visa 42.8% test figure from the earlier notes is NOT verified here, do not use.

articles.title: OpenAI startet ChatGPT Wallet: KI-Agenten kaufen für Nutzer ein

facts.text: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet on Friday, a payment method that lets its AI agents, called Dots, buy on users' behalf.
It was built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa so cardholders keep existing rewards and protections.
At first it is available only to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and over.
Users enter card details once; before purchase they review items, amount and card, then approve with Face ID or a fingerprint scan.
Dots get no direct access to card data; payment networks issue a per-transaction token with a card number, security code and expiry date.
OpenAI introduced Dots in late September.
Many websites and payment systems are not ready for agent purchases and may decline purchases made via the Wallet.
OpenAI is publishing a 'Commerce Partner Playbook' and says it works with Forter, Riskified, Sardine, Signifyd, Adyen, Checkout.com and Stripe.

stories.title: Apple launches an app to study how people use AI for health, with OpenEvidence
stories.notes: Same-day TechCrunch; The Verge also covered (unreadable). Related Bloomberg-via-AI Times item: Apple's first smart glasses (N50) to rely on Siri controlling iPhone apps, reveal targeted WWDC June 2027 (AI Times 217438); the Samsung-Google glasses post ran 11-13, so keep glasses separate.

articles.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health

facts.text: Apple is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app.
It invites US users over 21 with an iPhone 15 or later, iOS 26 or later and Apple Intelligence enabled.
Apple aims to run the study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.
Users can ask health questions with answers grounded in clinical data from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA and Nature.
Participants can share HealthKit data such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep or lab results for more personalized suggestions.
Data is anonymized before going to a secure third-party cloud provider and will not be used to train AI models; OpenEvidence deletes queries and responses after 24 hours.
The app is available to download starting today for US users.
The article notes OpenAI said earlier this year users asked over 300 million health-related queries each week.

stories.title: Uber driver licence data stolen via AI vendor Fireworks AI
stories.notes: TNW relays TechCrunch's original (not read). Single outlet.

articles.title: Uber driver licence data stolen via Fireworks AI

facts.text: Uber is warning drivers that hackers stole personal and driver's licence information from one of its vendors, which TechCrunch identified as Fireworks AI; Uber confirmed it.
Fireworks told Uber on 9 October that hackers had stolen internal credentials, which were then used to reach Uber's data.
State filings list 2,567 people in Massachusetts, 3,430 in South Carolina and 1,873 in Rhode Island, 7,870 so far; California and Illinois residents were notified without a count.
Fireworks, valued at $17.5bn in July, sells developers access to open AI models.
It disclosed two incidents in October; attackers took billing data and, for some customers, secrets, datasets and unfinished model weights.
Fireworks blamed a group that sells stolen access to AI models, a practice known as LLMjacking.
It is unclear why driver licence data sat with an AI inference provider; it is Uber's second known breach this year.

stories.title: SK Telecom and Hyosung Heavy Industries team up on AI data center power (345kV substations, 800V DC)
stories.notes: Korea Herald also covers (Google News, unread). Korean-language source. Few hard numbers. Earlier posts: SK Hyper 5GW (backlog 10-25) is a different story.

articles.title: SKT, 효성중공업과 AI 데이터센터 전력 인프라 맞손

facts.text: SK Telecom and Hyosung Heavy Industries signed an MOU on AI data center power equipment supply and demonstration of next-generation power technology, announced on the 16th.
They will build a stable supply system for key equipment such as 345kV substation gear.
A 345kV substation converts high-capacity grid power into voltage a data center can use.
Long-lead items such as transformers will have production and supply plans agreed early to reduce procurement uncertainty.
They will jointly study and demonstrate 800V DC power distribution, which sends DC power close to servers to cut conversion steps.
Cooperation may expand to gigawatt-class AI data center development; SKT CEO Jung Jai-hun said it will help secure core power infrastructure.

stories.title: Nvidia AI Day Seoul: 2,000+ attendees, physical AI and Korean developer communities

articles.title: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea's Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities

facts.text: More than 2,000 attendees came over two days at COEX for AI Day Seoul, focused on physical AI and AI agents.
Deepu Talla, Nvidia VP of robotics and edge AI, said Korea is 'punching above its weight'.
He named Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group, and startups Real World and Luda Robotics, as using Nvidia platforms.
More than 500 developers took part in full-day Deep Learning Institute workshops and certification exams in Korean.
Ten NVIDIA Inception startups pitched at the Physical AI Startup Connect event, including TwelveLabs, Avikus and Tesollo.
The Hangul Day hackathon winner, FlyGate, built agents on Korean language and culture and received an NVIDIA DGX Spark.

articles.title: Jensen Huang discusses Nvidia comeback, FT says
Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry?
Nvidia pressed Taiwan over indicted manager

facts.text: Jensen Huang has been discussing a possible comeback as Nvidia's CEO, days after the board pushed him out, the FT reported; he resigned on Thursday.
Brad Gerstner of Altimeter and Gavin Baker of Atreides, both Nvidia investors, urged the board to take a slow approach to choosing a successor, including 'the potential return of Jensen Huang'.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia needs a dramatic leadership shakeup and should look outside the company for its next chief.
The board's inquiry is run by Wachtell Lipton; Huang is expected to testify before Congress; Nvidia reports results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress.
Nvidia apparently accounts for roughly 80% of the AI GPU market.
Nvidia reported $99 billion in investments, another $25 billion in commitments and $36 billion in cloud service commitments, including CoreWeave, Nebius, OpenAI and Anthropic.
There was no succession plan in place, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
Prosecutors in Keelung, Taiwan call an indicted Nvidia manager the core figure in a network that sent 74 servers with Nvidia chips to China; another 56 were seized.
Nvidia said it found no indication its employee knew of the alleged diversion effort by employees at other companies.

stories.title: AI models took down a replica Polish wind farm in under two hours (security research)
stories.notes: Der Standard (Austria) article is partly paywalled; only the lede was readable. Needs the underlying research report before use. Weak: facts limited to the lede.

articles.title: Zu Forschungszwecken: KI-Modelle legen Windpark in unter zwei Stunden lahm

facts.text: In December last year, suspected Russian hackers attacked a Polish wind farm; they spent 11 days in the network before shutting the plant down.
Security experts recreated the incident for research and let two AI systems loose on a fictional wind farm.
The AI systems needed under two hours to take six turbines, with almost 10 megawatts of capacity, out of operation.
